title: Press Freedom Under Threat in Turkey
main_content:
A coalition of media rights groups says freedom of the press is under attack in Turkey.

The coalition’s representatives recently completed a visit to the country. They studied the government’s treatment of reporters and the press. The findings were released a month before Turkey’s general elections.

A crowd of supporters of the ruling party demonstrated near the offices of the Hurriyet newspaper last month. They were angry about an article in the newspaper.

The protesters claimed the story contained lies about Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. Days later, one of the newspaper’s columnists was attacked.

Melody Patry is with the group Index On Censorship. She was part of the delegation in Turkey.

“But Mohammed Rasool is just one example of the many other journalists and media workers who are being imprisoned and detained for simply doing their job, which is reporting the news, and that is not a crime.”

Mehmet Solmaz is the news editor of the Daily Sabah newspaper.

He says Turkish journalists often like to write about political issues when they should be reporting news and information.

questions.question: Why was there a crowd in front of the Hurriyet newspaper offices?
options: A protest against the government's censorship policies
Anger over a story about Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan
Support for a new editorial team at the newspaper
Celebration of a recent award won by the Hurriyet newspaper
questions.answer: Anger over a story about Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan

questions.question: Who said that press is under attack in Turkey?
options: A coalition of media rights groups
questions.answer: A coalition of media rights groups

questions.question: Who is Recep Tayyip Erdogan?
options: A representative from Index On Censorship
The editor of the Hurriyet newspaper
